correctness.rationale: Reconstruction: every connected component is a two-sided Z-path; every global graph automorphism maps each such component by j↦j+t or j↦t−j. Injective φ turns translation color equality into vertexwise identity. Reversal color equality forces the target sequence x′ to have period two via overlapping ordered pairs, excluded from the free set. If φ noninjective, one of six unordered binary pair collisions occurs; the table provides one of three explicitly aperiodic sequences and an integer reflection center for each case. Their entire color string is invariant by a point/adjacent-pair or step symmetry, and extending the local reflection by identity gives a global nontrivial Borel automorphism. Four input pairs yield precisely the stated palette count. The standalone checker tested all four-label rules against all six reflections across -30..30; the infinite proof is symbolic, not inferred from these tests.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-record and primary-literature searches requested two-block equivariant distinguishing rules, reflection symmetry, and the Chen–Zou theorem. Closest retrieved results concern ordinary chromatic colorings or unrelated coding invariants. value.rationale: The natural nearest-neighbor symbolic coding model for distinguishing the binary free shift has its complete admissible rule set and exact label threshold identified. Unrestricted Borel three-color distinguishability was established in 2026, leaving the genuinely different issue of whether that optimum can be implemented using only two adjacent symbols. The sharp four-vs-three gap and six collision obstructions explain why a purely two-cell local construction cannot realize the Borel optimum, a precise locality constraint for future symbolic-factor constructions. It is a small structural classification, not a claim about arbitrary continuous maps or higher-dimensional actions.
